## Choose an example

On **1. Data**, choose a **Packaged training example** and click **Load selected example**.
Provide one labeled dataset. On Features, Shiny divides it into training,
validation and test sets; no separate unlabeled file is required.
Loading or downloading data does not train a model. The app reads files from
the installed package, using `system.file("extdata", ..., package = "DDESONN")`.
Iris and mtcars come from R's datasets package. These choices work offline;
the GitHub source link is for browsing, not an automatic download fallback.

| Example | Suggested task / target | Starting predictors | Important context |
|---|---|---|---|
| Iris | Multiclass / Species | Four numeric measurements | Small first example, 150 rows. |
| mtcars | Regression / mpg | wt, hp | Small regression example, 32 rows. |
| Heart failure | Binary / DEATH_EVENT | All 12 numeric predictors | Repeated inputs limit evaluation; see the research vignette. |
| WMT prices | Regression / close | open, high, low, volume | Packaged snapshot; ordered splitting is suggested. This same-row illustration is not a validated forecast. |
| Customer labeled dataset | Multiclass / Segmentation | Age | Other columns contain categories or missing values; ID is not preselected. |

The full original rows and columns remain available for inspection and download.
The suggested predictors are complete numeric columns. No rows are silently
deleted, categories encoded, or missing values imputed. Prepare additional
predictors yourself before selecting them. In WMT, the date is nonnumeric and
adjusted close derives from close, so neither is preselected for this illustration.

## A first iris model

1. Keep Iris on Data; inspect its preview.
2. On **2. Features**, use target **Species**, the four measurement predictors,
   and **Multiclass classification**. Review the split and click **Prepare data**.
3. On **3. Build & Train**, keep **Basic**, try hidden-layer sizes `8` and
   **Epochs per model fit** `2`, then click **Train new model**.
4. On **4. Model / Results**, inspect the evaluations and predictions. Results
   depend on settings and seed; this is a small workflow example, not a performance claim.

For mtcars, load its example instead. The suggested target is mpg, predictors wt
and hp, and task Regression. You can change the suggestions on Features.
**Show full R code** follows your actual prepared data and settings after preparation.

## Read the same data in R

```{r load-r-examples, eval=FALSE}
data <- datasets::iris
# Or use the regression example:
data <- datasets::mtcars
```

```{r load-package-csv, eval=FALSE}
path <- system.file("extdata", "heart_failure_clinical_records.csv",
                    package = "DDESONN")
stopifnot(nzchar(path))
data <- read.csv(path, check.names = FALSE)
```

The app's generated recipes use the corresponding installed filename and record
a SHA256 check for packaged CSVs, so changed data is detected when reproducing a
recipe. Original packaged CSV downloads preserve their bytes. Iris/mtcars CSV
exports contain the dataset columns; R row names are not exported as predictors.
The existing data files are reused; no external datasets are added by this change.

## Predict using the unlabeled customer file

Train a customer model first, or load your compatible saved workbench bundle.
The customer training preset uses Age as a complete numeric starting predictor;
the matching test file also contains Age. Under **Model / Results → Saved models & predictions → Predict on new rows**,
click **Predict customer groups with completed model**, or download the optional
customer prediction CSV. These rows have no Segmentation labels; they are not
needed for the training, validation or test split. No pretrained
model is bundled or automatically loaded. The saved predictor names and finite
numeric values must match; incompatible data produces an error rather than
changing the trained model. Additional categorical or incomplete predictors
require the same preparation in both training and prediction data.

Loading another dataset clears preparation for a new model while preserving
completed models. A raw file without target labels is not automatically assigned
a fake target. The original CSV upload and prediction-upload paths remain available.

## Seeds, evaluation and related guides

A seed value of 42 is not 42 runs. Basic uses the Features seed for one run.
Custom's training seed list repeats complete training runs on the same prepared
split: `42,43` with Single model and 100 epochs means two 100-epoch runs, 200 total.
Neither random nor ordered splitting automatically groups duplicate inputs or
related subjects. The heart-failure split correction remains separate future work.

The app's contextual links take you to **Vignettes** for this guide, the
standard-AdaGrad research record, single-run/ensemble plot controls and ensemble
logs. Installed HTML guides open locally when present; otherwise the links open
their online source. All guide navigation preserves your current session.
